facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Eustreptospondylus was discovered in 1870 at the Summertown Brick Pit near Oxford, England.
facts.quote: In 1870, workers at the Summertown Brick Pit, just north of Oxford, England, found the skeleton of a theropod.

facts.statement: John Phillips described the Eustreptospondylus bones in 1871 without assigning a name at that time.
facts.quote: Phillips described the bones in 1871, but did not name them.

facts.statement: Eustreptospondylus remains the most complete large Jurassic theropod found in Europe.
facts.quote: Eustreptospondylus is still the most complete of any large Jurassic European theropod.

facts.statement: Alick Donald Walker established the genus and species Eustreptospondylus oxoniensis in 1964.
facts.quote: In 1964, Alick Donald Walker clarified matters by erecting a separate genus and species for the Oxford specimen: Eustreptospondylus oxoniensis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was recovered from the Callovian stage of the Oxford Clay Formation approximately 162 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, OUM J13558, was recovered by W. Parker from claystone in a marine layer of the Stewartby Member of the Oxford Clay Formation, which dates to the Callovian stage of the Jurassic period, approximately 162 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen represents a subadult individual.
facts.quote: It represents a subadult individual.

facts.statement: An estimate by Paul in 1988 suggests the subadult holotype was about 4.63 meters long and weighed about 218 kilograms.
facts.quote: according to an estimate by Paul in 1988 was about 4.63 m long and weighed about 218 kg.

facts.statement: Hypothetical adult estimates suggest Eustreptospondylus reached around 6 meters in length and 0.5 tons in mass.
facts.quote: Various estimates suggest that Eustreptospondylus was an "average-sized" theropod, with a hypothetical adult length of around 6 m, and a mass of 0.5 t.

facts.statement: The skull of Eustreptospondylus features a pointed snout and a large, horizontally oriented nostril.
facts.quote: The skull of Eustreptospondylus has a rather pointed snout in side view, with a large horizontally oriented nostril.

facts.statement: Oblique grooves in the jaw joints allowed Eustreptospondylus to widen its mouth gape when opening its lower jaws.
facts.quote: Oblique grooves in the jaw joints caused the gape of the mouth to be widened when the lower jaws were opened.

facts.statement: A shallow depression pierced by a smaller foramen is present in the corner of the lacrimal bone.
facts.quote: In the corner of the lacrimal a shallow depression is present, which is pierced by a smaller foramen.

facts.statement: The ilium features a 'brevis shelf' formed by the rear blade, which functions as an attachment area for the tail muscle Musculus caudofemoralis brevis.
facts.quote: With the rear blade of the ilium, the lower edge of the outer blade side is turned upwards to an almost horizontal position, creating and denuding over its total length a bone surface, the "brevis shelf", forming the internal face of the inner blade side — this shelf with dinosaurs functions as an attachment area for a tail muscle, the Musculus caudofemoralis brevis.

facts.statement: Eustreptospondylus is commonly classified as a member of the Eustreptospondylinae clade within the Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: Today Eustreptospondylus is commonly considered a member of the Eustreptospondylinae, clade within the Megalosauridae.

facts.statement: Because fossils were found on islands when Europe was an archipelago, Eustreptospondylus might have been capable of swimming short distances.
facts.quote: Eustreptospondylus is known from a fossil from what was an island, at a time when Europe consisted mostly of archipelagos. This suggests that it might have been able to swim short distances.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Eustreptospondylus was a swimmer or if its fossils were transported to the sea by floods or rivers after death.
facts.quote: Not all palaeontologists agree with the swimming hypothesis. The opposing theories hold that the fossil of Eustreptospondylus was either swept out to sea during a flood after the animal died on the mainland, or it was carried to the ocean after it died in a river.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Eustreptospondylus evolved insular dwarfism is debated, as some researchers argue the small size was due to the holotype being a subadult.
facts.quote: Eustreptospondylus has been portrayed as a genus that evolved insular dwarfism. In 2000, David Martill and Darren Naish pointed out that the portrayal of the animal as an island-dwelling dwarf species was caused by not realizing that the holotype specimen represented a subadult.

facts.statement: In 2003, Rauhut proposed that Eustreptospondylus oxoniensis should be classified as Magnosaurus oxoniensis.
facts.quote: In 2003 he proposed that they should be the same genus, which would make the full species name Magnosaurus oxoniensis.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul considered Eustreptospondylus oxoniensis identical to Streptospondylus altdorfensis.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul considered the species identical to Streptospondylus altdorfensis.

facts.statement: Eustreptospondylus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 164 to 161 million years ago, in the Callovian stage of what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 164 y 161 millones, en el Calloviense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: The holotype was a subadult measuring about 4.63 meters long and weighing 218 kilograms, suggesting an adult would reach about 6 meters in length and weigh half a ton.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Eustreptospondylus poseía una longitud de alrededor de 4,63 metros de largo y peso de alrededor de 218 kilogramos, pero es un subadulto, por lo que un ejemplar totalmente desarrollado habría medido alrededor de 6 metros y pesado 1/2 tonelada.

facts.statement: Eustreptospondylus was a bipedal carnivore with a slender tail, powerful hind legs, an erect posture, and small arms.
facts.quote: Fue un carnívoro bípedo que tenía una delgada cola. Su estructura es la de un terópodo típico, con poderosas patas traseras, postura erecta y brazos pequeños.

facts.statement: Unlike Megalosaurus, Eustreptospondylus had a thinner and more slender physical build.
facts.quote: A diferencia de Megalosaurus, posee una constitución física más delgada y esbelta.

facts.statement: The skull featured a quite pointed snout in side view with a large horizontally oriented nasal fossa.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Eustreptospondylus tiene un hocico bastante puntiagudo en vista lateral, con una gran fosa nasal orientada horizontalmente.

facts.statement: There is no lacrimal horn present in Eustreptospondylus.
facts.quote: No hay cuerno lagrimal.

facts.statement: Oblique slots in the jaw joints caused the mouth to widen when the lower jaws opened.
facts.quote: Las ranuras oblicuas en las articulaciones de la mandíbula causaron que la boca se ensanchara cuando se abrieron las mandíbulas inferiores.

facts.statement: Although not excavated, the front dorsal vertebrae have paired hypapophyses on their lower parts, similar to Streptospondylus altdorfensis.
facts.quote: Aunque no están excavadas, las vértebras dorsales delanteras tienen hipapofisis pareadas en sus partes inferiores, al igual que en Streptospondylus altdorfensis.

facts.statement: In 1870, workers at Summertown Brick Pit, just north of Oxford, England, found the skeleton of a theropod.
facts.quote: En 1870, los trabajadores de Summertown Brick Pit, justo al norte de Oxford, Inglaterra, encontraron el esqueleto de un terópodo.

facts.statement: Professor John Phillips described the bones in 1871 but did not name them at that time.
facts.quote: Phillips describió los huesos en 1871, pero no los nombró.

facts.statement: Eustreptospondylus remains the most complete of all large Jurassic European theropods.
facts.quote: Eustreptospondylus sigue siendo el más completo de todos los grandes terópodos jurásicos europeos.

facts.statement: The genus name Eustreptospondylus was intended to mean "true Streptospondylus".
facts.quote: El nombre del género Eustreptospondylus, fue pensado para significar " Streptospondylus verdadero ".

facts.statement: The specific name Oxoniensis refers to its origin from Oxford.
facts.quote: El nombre específico Oxoniensis, se refiere a su procedencia de Oxford.

facts.statement: The holotype OUM J13558 was recovered by W. Parker from clay in a marine layer of the Stewartby Member of the Oxford Clay Formation, dating to the Callovian stage of the Jurassic, about 162 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo, OUM J13558, fue recuperado por W. Parker a partir de arcilla en una capa marina del miembro Stewartby de la formación de Arcilla Oxford, que se remonta a la etapa Calloviense del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 162 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype was fully prepared and exhibited in 1924 in a fairly erect position.
facts.quote: El holotipo se preparó completamente y se exhibió en 1924, en una posición bastante erecta.

facts.statement: Since only one skeleton has been found, Eustreptospondylus was probably a rare theropod.
facts.quote: Como solo se ha encontrado un esqueleto, Eustreptospondylus fue probablemente un terópodo raro.

facts.statement: Today, Eustreptospondylus is commonly considered a member of Eustreptospondylinae, a clade within Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: Hoy en día, Eustreptospondylus se considera comúnmente un miembro de Eustreptospondylinae, clado dentro de Megalosauridae.

facts.statement: Like many other theropods, Eustreptospondylus fed on smaller dinosaurs and pterosaurs, or scavenged carcasses of fish, marine reptiles, and other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Eustreptospondylus, como muchos otros terópodos, se alimentaron de dinosaurios y pterosaurios más pequeños, o eliminaron los cadáveres de peces, reptiles marinos y otros dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Eustreptospondylus is known from a fossil found on an island when Europe consisted mainly of archipelagos.
facts.quote: Eustreptospondylus se conoce a partir de un fósil de una isla, en un momento en que Europa consistía principalmente de archipiélagos.

facts.statement: Eustreptospondylus has been considered a good swimmer, strong enough to swim from island to island like the modern Komodo dragon.
facts.quote: Eustreptospondylus ha sido considerado un buen nadador, lo suficientemente fuerte como para nadar de isla en isla como el moderno dragón de Komodo.

facts.statement: Not all paleontologists agree with the swimming hypothesis; opposing theories suggest the fossil was dragged to the sea during a flood after the animal died on the continent, or carried to the ocean after dying in a river.
facts.quote: No todos los paleontólogos están de acuerdo con la hipótesis de la natación. Las teorías opuestas sostienen que el fósil de Eustreptospondylus fue arrastrado al mar durante una inundación después de que el animal murió en el continente, o fue llevado al océano después de que murió en un río.

facts.statement: In 2000, researchers David Martill and Darren Naish argued that the animal was incorrectly described as an island dwarf because the holotype was actually a subadult.
facts.quote: En el 2000, David Martill y Darren Naish señalaron que la representación del animal como una especie de enano que habita en una isla fue causada por no darse cuenta de que el espécimen holotipo representaba un subadulto.

facts.quote: PBDB name: Eustreptospondylus (genus), Walker 1964

facts.statement: Eustreptospondylus belongs to the parent group Eustreptospondylinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Eustreptospondylinae

facts.quote: Family: Megalosauridae

facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
